paragraphs.title: Ascending to the Lord with Defined Boundaries

easy.question: Who was told to go up to the Lord?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The elders
easy.explanation: The passage begins: “And he said unto Moses.”

easy.question: Who was included among those going up with Moses?
answers: All the people
Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders
Joshua alone
easy.explanation: The passage names Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders.

easy.question: Who was not to go up with Moses?
answers: Aaron
The seventy elders
The people
easy.explanation: It states explicitly: “Neither shall the people go up with him.”

medium.question: What order of approach is described in the verses?
answers: The people approach first, followed by Moses
The group worships from a distance, and Moses approaches alone
The entire group approaches the Lord together
medium.explanation: First, the group is told to worship from a distance; then Moses approaches alone.

medium.question: What does “worship ye afar off” mean in context?
answers: Worship quickly
Worship silently
Worship from a place that is not near
medium.explanation: The phrase means to worship from a distance rather than approach as closely as Moses does.

medium.question: What difference between Moses and the rest of the group appears in the verses?
answers: Moses approaches the Lord alone, while the others do not approach in the same way
Moses does not go up at all, and the people go instead
Moses and the people go up to the same place together
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Moses approaches alone, while the others worship from a distance and the people do not go up with him.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “worship ye afar off” and “Moses alone shall come near”?
answers: The whole group was allowed to approach equally
Moses was not allowed to go up at all
There were different degrees of nearness: the group stayed distant, while Moses came closer alone
challenge.explanation: The contrast shows a difference in how closely each group could approach the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “alone” emphasize in “Moses alone shall come near the Lord”?
answers: Only Moses approached the Lord, not the other invited people
Moses did not go up at all
Moses approached together with all the people
challenge.explanation: “Alone” emphasizes that Moses approached by himself, unlike the others who were told not to come near.

challenge.question: How many people are included in the list Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders?
challenge.explanation: There are four individually named or identified people, plus seventy elders: 4 + 70 = 74.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “worship ye afar off” and “Moses alone shall come near”?
answers: The whole group was allowed to approach equally
Moses was not allowed to go up at all
There were different degrees of nearness: the group stayed distant, while Moses came closer alone
questions.explanation: The contrast shows a difference in how closely each group could approach the Lord.

questions.question: What does “alone” emphasize in “Moses alone shall come near the Lord”?
answers: Only Moses approached the Lord, not the other invited people
Moses did not go up at all
Moses approached together with all the people
questions.explanation: “Alone” emphasizes that Moses approached by himself, unlike the others who were told not to come near.

questions.question: How many people are included in the list Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders?
questions.explanation: There are four individually named or identified people, plus seventy elders: 4 + 70 = 74.

paragraphs.title: The People Receive the Lord’s Words

easy.question: Who told the people the Lord’s words and judgments?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says: “And Moses came and told the people.”

easy.question: How did all the people respond to the Lord’s words?
answers: They remained silent
They agreed and said they would do all the words
They asked to return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The people answered with one voice: “All the words which the Lord hath said will we do.”

easy.question: How many pillars did Moses set up?
answers: Ten
Seven
Twelve
easy.explanation: Moses set up twelve pillars, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel.

medium.question: Why were twelve pillars set up?
answers: To represent the twelve tribes of Israel
To mark the way through the wilderness
To count the sacrifices
medium.explanation: The verse says they were set up according to the twelve tribes of Israel.

medium.question: What did Moses do before building the altar?
answers: He sent Israelite young men
He wrote all the words of the Lord
He sacrificed oxen
medium.explanation: Moses first wrote the Lord’s words, and then rose early and built an altar.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the twelve pillars mentioned in the verse?
answers: They were stones or posts set up as a sign
They were tools for measuring time
They were special garments for priests
medium.explanation: The twelve pillars were set up as a sign representing the twelve tribes of Israel.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of events in the verses?
answers: Moses told the people, wrote the words, built an altar, and the people offered sacrifices
The people offered sacrifices, Moses wrote, and then he told the people
Moses built an altar, the people refused, and then Moses wrote the words
challenge.explanation: Moses first told the people, then wrote the Lord’s words, built the altar and pillars, and finally sent Israelite young men to offer sacrifices.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “all the people answered with one voice”?
answers: Only the leaders agreed
The people responded with united agreement
The people spoke several languages
challenge.explanation: “With one voice” emphasizes that the whole people responded together and agreed.

challenge.question: Which detail connects the altar with all the people of Israel?
answers: The altar was built in the morning
The sacrifices were oxen
Twelve pillars were set up beside the altar for the tribes
challenge.explanation: The twelve pillars represented all twelve tribes, connecting the covenant ceremony with the entire people.

questions.question: What is the correct order of events in the verses?
answers: Moses told the people, wrote the words, built an altar, and the people offered sacrifices
The people offered sacrifices, Moses wrote, and then he told the people
Moses built an altar, the people refused, and then Moses wrote the words
questions.explanation: Moses first told the people, then wrote the Lord’s words, built the altar and pillars, and finally sent Israelite young men to offer sacrifices.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “all the people answered with one voice”?
answers: Only the leaders agreed
The people responded with united agreement
The people spoke several languages
questions.explanation: “With one voice” emphasizes that the whole people responded together and agreed.

questions.question: Which detail connects the altar with all the people of Israel?
answers: The altar was built in the morning
The sacrifices were oxen
Twelve pillars were set up beside the altar for the tribes
questions.explanation: The twelve pillars represented all twelve tribes, connecting the covenant ceremony with the entire people.

paragraphs.title: Half the Blood on the Altar

easy.question: Who took half of the blood?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says: “And Moses took half of the blood.”

easy.question: Where did Moses put half of the blood?
answers: On the altar
In basins
In the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses put half of the blood in basins.

easy.question: What did Moses do with the other half of the blood?
answers: He poured it on the ground
He kept it in the basins
He sprinkled it on the altar
easy.explanation: The verse says: “And half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.”

medium.question: What was the order of Moses’ actions in the verse?
answers: He took half the blood, put it in basins, and sprinkled the other half on the altar
He sprinkled all the blood on the altar and then took half of it
He put all the blood in basins and then sprinkled it on the altar
medium.explanation: Moses first took half the blood and put it in basins, then sprinkled the other half on the altar.

medium.question: What were the basins used for in “he put it in basins”?
answers: Small altars
Containers or bowls
Special garments
medium.explanation: Basins are containers or bowls; the context says Moses put the blood in them.

medium.question: How was the blood divided according to the verse?
answers: Most was put in basins and a little was sprinkled on the altar
All of it was put in basins and only later sprinkled
Half was put in basins and half was sprinkled on the altar
medium.explanation: The verse mentions half the blood for each of two different actions.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repetition of “half of the blood”?
answers: The blood was divided into two equal parts
Moses used only a small amount of blood
The blood was poured in three places
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to both portions, showing that the blood was divided into two equal parts.

challenge.question: What difference between the two portions of blood is described?
answers: The first was poured out and the second was taken
The first was put in basins and the second was sprinkled on the altar
The first was burned and the second was saved
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes between putting one half in basins and sprinkling the other half on the altar.

challenge.question: Which statement is accurate according to the verse alone?
answers: The verse says Moses divided the blood between Moses and Aaron
The verse says all the blood was sprinkled on the altar
The verse describes a different action for each half of the blood
challenge.explanation: One half was put in basins, while the other half was sprinkled on the altar; the verse does not describe dividing it between people.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repetition of “half of the blood”?
answers: The blood was divided into two equal parts
Moses used only a small amount of blood
The blood was poured in three places
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to both portions, showing that the blood was divided into two equal parts.

questions.question: What difference between the two portions of blood is described?
answers: The first was poured out and the second was taken
The first was put in basins and the second was sprinkled on the altar
The first was burned and the second was saved
questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes between putting one half in basins and sprinkling the other half on the altar.

questions.question: Which statement is accurate according to the verse alone?
answers: The verse says Moses divided the blood between Moses and Aaron
The verse says all the blood was sprinkled on the altar
The verse describes a different action for each half of the blood
questions.explanation: One half was put in basins, while the other half was sprinkled on the altar; the verse does not describe dividing it between people.

paragraphs.title: The Book of the Covenant and the Covenant Blood

easy.question: What did the people say after Moses read the Book of the Covenant to them?
answers: All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient
We will not do the Lord’s words
We will obey only part of the words
easy.explanation: The people said: “All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient.”

easy.question: What did Moses read to the people?
answers: The book of the law
The Book of the Covenant
A list of Israel’s names
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people.

easy.question: What did Moses sprinkle on the people?
answers: Water
Oil
Blood
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people.

medium.question: What happened immediately after the people said, “All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient”?
answers: Moses sprinkled the blood on the people
The people left the place
Moses wrote a new book
medium.explanation: After the people responded, Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on them.

medium.question: What does “be obedient” mean in the statement “All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient”?
answers: We will listen and obey
We will sing aloud
We will sleep quietly
medium.explanation: Together with “will we do,” the phrase means that the people would listen to the Lord’s words and obey them.

medium.question: Why was the blood called “the blood of the covenant”?
answers: Because it was poured out instead of the Book of the Covenant
Because it was a sign of the covenant the Lord made with the people
Because the people asked to drink it
medium.explanation: Moses explained that the blood was the blood of the covenant the Lord made with the people concerning all these words.

challenge.question: Which combination of actions is described in the verses?
answers: The people accepted the Lord’s words verbally, and Moses marked the covenant with blood
Moses refused to read, and the people offered a sacrifice
The people wrote the covenant, and Moses listened to it
challenge.explanation: The people declared that they would keep the Lord’s words, and Moses then used the blood as a sign of the covenant.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “concerning all these words”?
answers: The covenant applied to only some of the words
The covenant concerned all the words that had been spoken
The words were spoken only to Moses
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the covenant concerned everything that had been said to the people.

challenge.question: Who said each of the central statements in the verses?
answers: Moses said the people’s words, and the people said Moses’ words
The people said “We will do and be obedient,” and Moses said, “Behold the blood of the covenant”
They both said both statements together
challenge.explanation: The people made the promise to obey, and Moses declared, “Behold the blood of the covenant.”

questions.question: Which combination of actions is described in the verses?
answers: The people accepted the Lord’s words verbally, and Moses marked the covenant with blood
Moses refused to read, and the people offered a sacrifice
The people wrote the covenant, and Moses listened to it
questions.explanation: The people declared that they would keep the Lord’s words, and Moses then used the blood as a sign of the covenant.

questions.question: What can be understood from the words “concerning all these words”?
answers: The covenant applied to only some of the words
The covenant concerned all the words that had been spoken
The words were spoken only to Moses
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the covenant concerned everything that had been said to the people.

questions.question: Who said each of the central statements in the verses?
answers: Moses said the people’s words, and the people said Moses’ words
The people said “We will do and be obedient,” and Moses said, “Behold the blood of the covenant”
They both said both statements together
questions.explanation: The people made the promise to obey, and Moses declared, “Behold the blood of the covenant.”

paragraphs.title: The Elders’ Vision before the Lord

easy.question: Who went up with Moses?
answers: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders
Joshua and the entire tribe of Levi
Pharaoh and all his servants
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders.

easy.question: What did they see beneath the feet of the God of Israel?
answers: A smoking mountain
Something like a paved work of sapphire stone and the clear sky
A great stormy sea
easy.explanation: The passage describes what was beneath His feet as something like sapphire stone and the clear sky.

easy.question: What did the people do at the end of the passage?
answers: They built an altar
They came down from the mountain
They ate and drank
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying: “They did eat and drink.”

medium.question: What can be understood from the statement that the Lord “laid not his hand” on the nobles of Israel?
answers: They saw God and were not harmed
They did not go up the mountain
They hid and saw nothing
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that although they saw God, they were not struck or harmed.

medium.question: Who were the “nobles” mentioned in the passage?
answers: Poor people
Leaders or honored people
Foreign soldiers
medium.explanation: The word refers to important or honored leaders among the people of Israel.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the verses?
answers: They ate, then went up, and finally saw
They saw, then went up, and finally drank
They went up, saw the God of Israel, and then ate and drank
medium.explanation: First they went up, then they saw the God of Israel, and finally they ate and drank.

challenge.question: How many people are explicitly mentioned as going up with Moses, counting Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders?
challenge.explanation: Besides Moses, there are Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu—three people—plus seventy elders. Together with Moses, the total is 74.

challenge.question: What central contrast appears in the passage?
answers: They saw God, yet were not harmed and even ate and drank
They did not see God, so they ran away
They saw God, so they stopped eating and drinking
challenge.explanation: The passage describes both a vision of God and the fact that they were unharmed and continued eating and drinking.

challenge.question: What does the comparison to “the body of heaven in his clearness” emphasize?
answers: Darkness and danger
Brightness, clarity, and purity
Heat and fire
challenge.explanation: The reference to the clear sky emphasizes a bright, pure, and transparent appearance.

questions.question: How many people are explicitly mentioned as going up with Moses, counting Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders?
questions.explanation: Besides Moses, there are Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu—three people—plus seventy elders. Together with Moses, the total is 74.

questions.question: What central contrast appears in the passage?
answers: They saw God, yet were not harmed and even ate and drank
They did not see God, so they ran away
They saw God, so they stopped eating and drinking
questions.explanation: The passage describes both a vision of God and the fact that they were unharmed and continued eating and drinking.

questions.question: What does the comparison to “the body of heaven in his clearness” emphasize?
answers: Darkness and danger
Brightness, clarity, and purity
Heat and fire
questions.explanation: The reference to the clear sky emphasizes a bright, pure, and transparent appearance.

paragraphs.title: Moses Is Called to Receive the Tablets

easy.question: Who did the Lord tell to go up the mountain?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The Lord said to Moses: “Come up to me into the mount.”

easy.question: What was Moses to receive on the mountain?
answers: The tabernacle
The tables of stone, the law, and the commandments
The priestly garments
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would give Moses the tables of stone, the law, and the commandments.

easy.question: Who went up with Moses to the mountain of God?
answers: Aaron
Hur
Joshua, his minister
easy.explanation: The verse says: “Moses rose up, and his minister Joshua; and Moses went up.”

medium.question: Why did Moses tell the elders to stay where they were until he returned?
answers: Because he was going up the mountain for a time
Because they had to build an altar
Because they were waiting for Pharaoh
medium.explanation: Moses told them to remain there until he returned from the mountain.

medium.question: In “Tarry ye here for us,” what does “here” mean?
answers: In the wilderness
In this place
In the house
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the elders should remain in the place where they were.

medium.question: What were Aaron and Hur to do while Moses was on the mountain?
answers: Lead the people to the mountain
Write the law
Handle the people’s matters and concerns
medium.explanation: Moses said that anyone with a matter should go to Aaron and Hur.

challenge.question: What can be understood from Moses going up with Joshua while leaving the elders below?
answers: Joshua served and accompanied Moses, while the elders remained to lead the people
Joshua was the high priest
The elders were forbidden to speak with the people
challenge.explanation: Joshua is called Moses’ minister, while the elders were left to remain and handle the people’s affairs.

challenge.question: What does “that thou mayest teach them” show about the purpose of the law and commandments?
answers: They were only decorations for the stone tablets
They were intended to teach and guide the people
They were meant to hide the Lord’s words
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the law and commandments were intended to instruct and guide the people.

challenge.question: Why did Moses specifically mention Aaron and Hur rather than simply tell the elders to wait?
answers: To identify them as leaders responsible for the people’s affairs while he was away
To say that they would go up the mountain before him
To announce that they would receive the stone tablets
challenge.explanation: Moses appointed Aaron and Hur as the people’s points of contact while he was on the mountain.

questions.question: What can be understood from Moses going up with Joshua while leaving the elders below?
answers: Joshua served and accompanied Moses, while the elders remained to lead the people
Joshua was the high priest
The elders were forbidden to speak with the people
questions.explanation: Joshua is called Moses’ minister, while the elders were left to remain and handle the people’s affairs.

questions.question: What does “that thou mayest teach them” show about the purpose of the law and commandments?
answers: They were only decorations for the stone tablets
They were intended to teach and guide the people
They were meant to hide the Lord’s words
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the law and commandments were intended to instruct and guide the people.

questions.question: Why did Moses specifically mention Aaron and Hur rather than simply tell the elders to wait?
answers: To identify them as leaders responsible for the people’s affairs while he was away
To say that they would go up the mountain before him
To announce that they would receive the stone tablets
questions.explanation: Moses appointed Aaron and Hur as the people’s points of contact while he was on the mountain.

paragraphs.title: The Cloud and the Glory of the Lord on Mount Sinai

easy.question: Who went up the mountain?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says: “Moses went up into the mount.”

easy.question: What covered the mountain?
answers: Fire
The cloud
Water
easy.explanation: The verses say that the cloud covered the mountain.

easy.question: What was the sight of the Lord’s glory at the top of the mountain like?
answers: A strong wind
Flowing water
Devouring fire
easy.explanation: The glory of the Lord was like “devouring fire on the top of the mount.”

medium.question: What happened on the seventh day?
answers: The cloud disappeared
The Lord called to Moses from within the cloud
The Israelites went up the mountain
medium.explanation: After the cloud covered the mountain for six days, the Lord called to Moses on the seventh day.

medium.question: What does “the glory of the Lord abode upon mount Sinai” mean?
answers: It rested or remained there
It fled from the place
It descended quickly
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord’s glory rested or remained on Mount Sinai.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The Lord called Moses, Moses went up, and then the cloud covered the mountain
The mountain burned, the people went up, and then Moses came down
Moses went up, the cloud covered the mountain, and on the seventh day the Lord called him
medium.explanation: This is the order described in the verses.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the sight of the Lord’s glory was visible to the Israelites?
answers: The cloud covered the mountain
Moses went up the mountain
The sight was in the eyes of the children of Israel
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the sight was in the eyes of the children of Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the Lord calling Moses only on the seventh day?
answers: Moses waited six days before the Lord called him
Moses did not go up the mountain
The Israelites waited only one day
challenge.explanation: The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and the Lord called Moses on the seventh day.

challenge.question: What does the comparison of the Lord’s glory to “devouring fire” emphasize?
answers: That the mountain was cold and dark
That the sight was powerful and awe-inspiring
That the fire was used for cooking
challenge.explanation: The comparison describes a powerful and impressive sight at the top of the mountain.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the sight of the Lord’s glory was visible to the Israelites?
answers: The cloud covered the mountain
Moses went up the mountain
The sight was in the eyes of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the sight was in the eyes of the children of Israel.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the Lord calling Moses only on the seventh day?
answers: Moses waited six days before the Lord called him
Moses did not go up the mountain
The Israelites waited only one day
questions.explanation: The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and the Lord called Moses on the seventh day.

questions.question: What does the comparison of the Lord’s glory to “devouring fire” emphasize?
answers: That the mountain was cold and dark
That the sight was powerful and awe-inspiring
That the fire was used for cooking
questions.explanation: The comparison describes a powerful and impressive sight at the top of the mountain.

easy.question: Who entered into the cloud?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says: “Moses went into the midst of the cloud.”

easy.question: Where did Moses go up?
answers: Into the wilderness
Into the mountain
To the sea
easy.explanation: The verse says: “He gat him up into the mount.”

easy.question: How long was Moses on the mountain?
answers: Seven days
Thirty days
Forty days and forty nights
easy.explanation: The verse states that Moses was in the mountain forty days and forty nights.

medium.question: What was the order of events in the verse?
answers: Moses entered the cloud and then went up the mountain
Moses came down from the mountain and then entered the cloud
Moses slept on the mountain and then came down
medium.explanation: The verse first says that Moses entered the cloud, and then that he went up into the mountain.

medium.question: What does “Moses went into the midst of the cloud” mean?
answers: He stayed outside the cloud
He went inside the cloud
He went above the cloud
medium.explanation: The phrase says that Moses entered into the middle of the cloud rather than remaining outside it.

medium.question: What can be understood from Moses being on the mountain forty days and forty nights?
answers: He stayed there only a short time
He went up only at night
He remained there for an extended, continuous period
medium.explanation: Mentioning forty days and forty nights emphasizes Moses’ long stay on the mountain, day and night.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Moses not only reached the mountain but remained there?
answers: The statement “Moses was in the mount”
The word “cloud”
The word “went up” alone
challenge.explanation: The statement that Moses was in the mountain describes his remaining there, not merely his arrival.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “forty days and forty nights” emphasize?
answers: The stay was only during the daytime
The stay continued through both day and night
Moses stayed on the mountain during two separate periods
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both days and nights emphasizes the full and continuous duration of his stay.

challenge.question: Which sequence most accurately describes Moses’ movement in the verse?
answers: He went up the mountain, came down, and entered the cloud
He entered the cloud, came down the mountain, and stayed in the wilderness
He entered the cloud, went up the mountain, and remained there for an extended time
challenge.explanation: The verse describes entering the cloud, going up the mountain, and then staying there forty days and forty nights.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Moses not only reached the mountain but remained there?
answers: The statement “Moses was in the mount”
The word “cloud”
The word “went up” alone
questions.explanation: The statement that Moses was in the mountain describes his remaining there, not merely his arrival.

questions.question: What does the phrase “forty days and forty nights” emphasize?
answers: The stay was only during the daytime
The stay continued through both day and night
Moses stayed on the mountain during two separate periods
questions.explanation: Mentioning both days and nights emphasizes the full and continuous duration of his stay.

questions.question: Which sequence most accurately describes Moses’ movement in the verse?
answers: He went up the mountain, came down, and entered the cloud
He entered the cloud, came down the mountain, and stayed in the wilderness
He entered the cloud, went up the mountain, and remained there for an extended time
questions.explanation: The verse describes entering the cloud, going up the mountain, and then staying there forty days and forty nights.
